To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the combination of cytogenetic techniques, including chromosome analysis and FISH, is needed in order to identify complex chromosome abnormalities, and (2) the combination of chromosome and FISH analysis with microarray analysis is necessary to identify the full extent of genomic changes in complex chromosome abnormalities

the use of multiple technologies in complex cases is necessary for accurate interpretation and understanding of the underlying chromosomal abnormalities and that the use of microarray alone is insufficient to fully understand the underlying chromosomal changes.
The combination of chromosome analysis and microarray analysis is essential in the evaluation of many patients with complex chromosomal abnormalities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of tools and technologies for the detection and analysis of complex genomic changes in cancer.
the use of multiple technologies to better understand the genomic complexity of the cases we see and the need to use the tools in our toolbox.
the application of cytogenetic technology to the diagnosis of chromosomal abnormalities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

chromosome analysis, FISH and microarray analysis are complementary technologies that are essential for a full understanding of the genomic picture and should be used as needed for a complete understanding of the chromosomal picture.
the array is an important tool to have in your cytogenetic toolbox, but it is not the only tool.
microarray analysis and FISH analysis are complementary technologies and both are required to fully characterize the genomic complexity of the cases presented.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chromosome analysis, FISH and microarray are complementary tools for understanding genomic abnormalities.

the array is a powerful tool for the analysis of chromosomal abnormalities, but the array is only one tool in the toolbox and should be utilized with chromosome and FISH analyses to obtain a comprehensive genomic picture of the patient.
chromosome analysis is essential to identify complex chromosome rearrangements, while the microarray is essential to identify copy number variations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of multiple cytogenetic technologies in the evaluation of complex cases will provide a more comprehensive understanding of the chromosomal changes present in the patient.
chromosome analysis is not a “dying” art.
the use of multiple technologies in the cytogenetic laboratory is critical in order to fully understand the genomic picture and provide the best possible care for the patients.
